ModMetaData.name: JustTerminal
ModMetaData.author: tiagocc0
ModMetaData.description:
A terminal inside the game, with an old CRT screen look. Type commands to see your colonists, factions and the colony.
Click the terminal button at the bottom bar to open it. Type help to see the commands, help and a command name shows examples for it. manual opens the manual, take your time with it, manual programming is the second part about writing your own programs.
pawns, pawn, why (a colonist's thoughts), rooms, trade (what traders carry), caravans, bills, colony, fetch, date, factions, critical (wounds nobody treated yet), checkup (diseases and treated wounds), visitors, danger (enemies and predators) and idle show what's going on. Pipes work too, like pawns | grep Sleeping, and watch 5 danger runs it again every 5 seconds.
rimtop (or top) is a colony monitor like btop: mood, temperature and wealth graphs, power and weather, stock, and the colonists listed like processes. Enter or a click shows a colonist's details, tab switches between the four boxes and one of them on the whole screen.
graph draws graphs over time: temperature outside (with a forecast), wealth, mood of the colony or of one colonist, food, colonists and raid points.
The normal commands only read. Type edit to go into edit mode, the screen turns red and the commands there change your colonists: work priorities, medicine, allowed area, policies, ideoligion roles (it opens the ritual), exile and caravans. You can make groups, like group miners Drill Wolf Kovul and then work @miners mining 1. draft, undraft and schedule are there too, and storage can copy what one stockpile takes to every shelf or the ones in a room.
research picks the next project, prisoner sets what the wardens do, hunt, tame, slaughter, master and train are for animals, bed gives out beds, switch sends someone to turn things on or off, and forbid and allow work on what's in storage.
pick hides the terminal and pauses the game so you can click a spot on the map, it tells you the x,z. place save gate pick keeps that spot with a name, and goto @guards gate drafts the guards and sends them there.
There are files too, kept in the save and not on your computer: ls, cd, mkdir, cat, less, cp, mv, rm and nano to write them. The folders under / are the game itself, read only, like cat /stock/food or ls /pawns/Tasca.
Files that end in .sh are programs. Most commands are programs you can read in /bin, copy to ~/bin and change, or you can write your own. The language is simple: for, if, print, and set to change things in edit mode.
Files that end in .cron are cron scripts. They check something every few hours, or run when something happens like a raid, a colonist going down or someone with a certain gene showing up, and then send a message, a letter or run a command or a program. Like this one:
every 2h fire daily if /stock/food < 3 action letter only {value} days of food left
cron lists them, cron_edit turns them on and off with the keys. example lists some .cron and .sh files to start from and copies them to your files.
The mod options can export the files and programs of a game and import them into another.
Click the little pin light on the top of the frame and it stays open when you click the map, and you can drag it around. In the mod options you can make your own theme: colors, effects, font, text size, the welcome text, commands to run when it starts and your own names for the commands.
There's also snake.
You can add it mid playthrough. To remove it from a playthrough, turn off saving in the mod options and save first.
The font is DejaVu Sans Mono, its license is in Common/Fonts.
AI was used to help code/fix issues
Non Steam version: https://github.com/purpleorangegames/JustTerminal
